Recently I stuck on old reddit comment with various interesting mod tools ideas (which are currently not implemented in reddit AFAIK, so this could be an advantage). Some of them are quite good to think over:

We have a moderation log that all moderators can view, yet there is no way to make it public.

The ability to leave a PM to a poster whos post is removed without having to make multiple clicks

Domain banning. You'd be amazed at how abusive NSFW sites can be with their spam.

controlling posts per day/year/timeframe a user can make. Some user take karma a little too seriously

The ability to remove moderators that sit above you on the moderator list through anonymous voting. Too often does a moderator leave reddit as a whole and their account gets hacked into and runs amuck. If they are the head mod, the whole subreddit goes to shit and admins rarely intervene.

https://www.reddit.com/r/worldnews/comments/1ywspe/new_snowden_doc_reveals_how_gchqnsa_use_the/cfp1kf3

Thank you for the ideas.

  • Ability to make the public moderation log is already in the todo list link to github issue
  • Posters already automatically receive a PM when their post is removed. What this needs is a quick way for the mod to add a personal message if he/she wants to do so.
  • Domain banning is already implemented on a site-wide level, further expanding this tool and letting sub moderators use it shouldn't be a problem. There is already a similar GitHub issue open which will cover this.
  • Removing moderators with higher power level through anonymous moderator voting sounds like a reasonable idea. I'd like to hear more input from community on this one since it may be abused (everything can be abused at some point?) but I'm definitely on board.

It's great that most of these are planned already!

I think there should be some time restrictions, i.e. if we talk about mods voting, then they should be subverse mods for n days before (at least month?).

The decision should be unanimous, maybe? Or at least 2/3 votes, maybe more.
Hypothetical: what happens if a sub recruits more mods with the unstated purpose of unseating a superior? Just trying to think of the abuse side.

Yeah, this idea is quite dangerous :) I was thinking more about community voting to dethrone a despot mod when copypasted it ;)

Personally I think it is a great idea. I've seen some things recently with Fleddit that this 100% addresses. But with great power...

My personal idea is to remove/demote mods for under-activity: let's say there are 10 mods, so then if some mods do less than 5% of all mod actions per month, they should be removed or at least transferred to the bottom.
